newsitem.title: UK: Bonds linked to MoD housing rents due soon - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bonds linked to MoD housing rents due soon - dealers.

text.p: Annington Homes, the consortium which bought nearly 58,000 British Ministry of Defence married quarters, will next week launch bond issues linked to rental payments on the properties, syndicate managers said on Tuesday.
Dealers said special purpose firm Annington Securities plc will issue three securitised bonds totalling 863 million stg.
A 330 million stg FRN with an average life of around five years was expected, as well as two fixed-rate bonds.
These would be a 173 million stg deal with a 12.5-year average life and a 360 million stg issue with an average life of 20 years.
All tranches were expected to receive a top-notch triple-A rating, dealers said.
HSBC and Nomura are arranging the transaction.
"The issue is expected to surface in the middle of next week," said a syndicate manager familiar with the deal.
"The fixed-rate tranches are likely to be bought by British institutions, but the FRN will have broader appeal," he said.
The MoD sold 57,400 married quarters for 1.662 billion stg to Annington last month in a deal underwritten by Nomura International.
Annington will offer army personnel attractively-priced mortgages and discounted prices to buy houses from the group, the MoD said at the time.
The deal comes under the government's so-called private finance initiative which aims to shift the capital cost and risk of public investments into public hands.
